assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Sr lattice demonstration with Ye's realisation of clocks at the 10^-18 level, with spectroscopy of a quality that sets the standard for precision measurement. Originality is high (Lamb-Dicke confinement without light shifts), the discovery is clear, and the impact reaches metrology, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. From an atomic-physics and measurement viewpoint this is the most compelling case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first Sr demonstrations; Ye drove the systematic accuracy and stability to the current record levels and the many-body and Sr-lattice clock extensions. Two laureates fit the supplied credit cleanly; Hall/Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) are adjacent prior recognition, so the novelty of the clock step has to be argued, but it is a distinct invention. Other contributors (for example early lattice-clock proposal contributors, from memory) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups worldwide and by international clock comparisons; the interpretation is stable and the technology is mature. Recognition is timely, with the redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel committee views optical clocks as sufficiently distinct from earlier recognised frequency-comb and ion-trap metrology work.
Exact precedence between early lattice-clock proposals and demonstrations is from memory and not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation (including teleportation, entanglement of many ions and error-corrected operations in Innsbruck) established a leading platform for quantum computation. Importance and lasting impact are very high, and the physics is well within coherent light-matter control that I know from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal; Blatt led key early experimental realisations. Wineland's group (already recognised in 2012 for ion control) and others (Monroe, Wineland, Häffner) did closely related work not credited here, so the three-person split raises an overlap question with the 2012 award. The credited trio is otherwise a natural configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by multiple trapped-ion groups and commercial efforts; stable interpretation. Timing is reasonable though the platform is still evolving toward fault tolerance.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with Monroe/Wineland contributions not in the supplied credit.
B019 and B031 list the same people; I treat B031 as the more specific, concrete invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED transferred cavity-QED strong coupling to superconducting circuits and made on-chip quantum control and readout routine, underpinning the major superconducting quantum computers. Originality and impact are high, and the link to atomic and quantum optics is direct.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf have the central proposal and first strong-coupling demonstration, which is a clean three-person configuration. Contributions from Devoret and others overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum phenomena in circuits, creating possible redundancy.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and mature; technology applications continue. The 2025 prize may reduce urgency for another superconducting-circuit award.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2025 Nobel Prize recognition of superconducting-circuit quantum effects (from my memory, not verified here).
Whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery or part of a single field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical addressing and coherent control of single spins in diamond and related solid-state colour centres created a platform for quantum sensing, networking and memories. It is an important solid-state analogue of atomic coherent control, and my rare-earth-crystal background gives me a good sense of the physics involved. Originality is real, though it is a broad field of work rather than a single sharp discovery.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup demonstrated single NV-spin detection and control, Awschalom developed coherent spin control and extended it to other defects, and Lukin led NV sensing and network concepts. Walsworth and others are also credited, so the proposed trio omits important contributors; the boundary is fuzzy.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and active applications; maturity is good for the core spin-control results, less so for the network applications.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested across a large community, and a three-person limit leaves out significant contributors.
Breadth of the topic may make a focused citation hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices, with the superfluid-Mott transition and the Hubbard-model quantum simulator programme, opened a general route for studying many-body quantum physics, including quantum-gas microscopy. Strong lasting impact and well confirmed. It builds on the 2001 and 1997 prizes in the field.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the theoretical proposal, Greiner and Bloch the key experiments (Mott transition, microscopy). The supplied credit includes Cirac, but Zoller overlaps with B031, so a prize combining this and B031 would double-count him.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups, mature and stable. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap in laureates with B031 and B019.
Possible concern that recognition of cold-atom physics is already substantial in earlier prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a foundational idea in quantum information whose protocols (BB84, E91) led to secure communication experiments and commercial systems. Importance is high and conceptually clear. The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments partly covers the foundations, but QKD itself was not cited.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84, Ekert of the entanglement-based protocol. Jian-Wei Pan's experimental satellite and network work is credited but would make a fourth laureate; the three theorists are the cleanest group.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are well established and demonstrated; practical security and implementation loopholes remain, but the principle is confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this a physics discovery versus an information-theory protocol.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene gave an extraordinarily tunable platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity, and spawned the entire field of twistronics. Impact is large and growing, and the discovery is conceptually elegant.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observation. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cory Dean and others contributed essential related work not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation exists, but the nature of superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet fully settled.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of superconductivity is unresolved.
Others who made contemporaneous experiments are not in the credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays with optical tweezers provide a new route to quantum simulation and computation, with fast-moving demonstrations of many-body phases and gates. Related to my interests in coherent light-matter interactions in a sense, but the field is moving quickly.
assessment.attribution: Lukin, Browaeys and Saffman each contributed to the demonstration of blockade-based gates and large arrays; Zoller's theoretical contributions overlap with other candidates. The split is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly developing; independent confirmation exists but the field is probably too recent for a prize.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the other atomic and quantum-information candidates.
Credit allocation among several leading groups is unsettled.
